figures.caption: Figure 3. Visualization of PCA subspace. The residual stream hidden states are taken from Llama-3.1-8B at layer 11 after the attention module (11 mid). The hidden states of P+ and P− are colored as blue and red. Arrows indicate the direction from one hidden state of P+ to the corresponding hidden state of P−. It can be seen that positive and negative hidden states are approximately linearly separable by one direction.

Figure 7. Path Patching and Attention Sink Ablation results on Mistral-7B. X axis indicates the center layer that we ablate or patch. Y axis is negation accuracy. Both methods suggest that mid-layer attention modules are causally important for negation processing.

Figure 5. Normalized evidence count plotted against attention layer index. The normalized evidence count measures the percentage of samples in the dataset for which evidence is identified at a given layer. Results are on Llama-3.1-8B. The blue (red) line indicates the ratio of samples that LogitLens identifies Ȳ (Y ) related tokens as top promoted (demoted) tokens. We observe that evidence count peaks at causally important attention modules.

Figure 6. Path Patching and Attention Sink Ablation results on Llama-3.1-8B. X axis indicates the center layer that we ablate or patch. Y axis is negation accuracy. Both methods suggest that mid-layer attention modules are causally important for negation processing.

Table 8. Best layer (1-indexed) for Attention Sink and LogitLens on each model, together with the best negative accuracy (%) achieved at that layer. Num Layers is the total number of hidden layers L reported by the model configuration.

Figure 10. Visualization of the PCA space at different model layers. The hidden states of P+ and P− are colored as blue and red. Arrows indicate the direction from one hidden state of P+ to the corresponding hidden state of P−. It can be seen that positive and negative hidden states are approximately linearly separable by one direction.

Table 5. Example of one data entry in our dataset. Each data entry contains a pair of prompts: 1) the positive (affirmative) prompt, 2) the negative prompt. Each entry also comes with a pair of gold answers for each prompt.
Table 6. Illustration of the four prompt templates used for negation sensitivity analysis.

Figure 9. Normalized evidence count plotted against attention layer index. Results are on mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1. The blue (red) line indicates the ratio of samples that LogitLens identifies Ȳ (Y ) related tokens as top promoted (demoted) tokens. We observe that evidence count for “not” follows the same trends as patching results in Figure 7.
Figure 2. OLMo2 Positive and Negative Accuracies at various pre-training checkpoints. We observe that negative accuracy first plummets at early training steps, then rises again and stabilizes.

Table 7. Multi-answer evaluation. Negative accuracy, positive accuracy, and sensitivity are computed using averaged logits over multiple candidate answers per prompt. All values are reported as percentages (%) with three significant figures.

Figure 8. Cross-validated LDA model accuracy as a function of position in the residual stream. A higher accuracy indicates that we can decode “not” from the residual stream more reliably. As shown, “not” is moved to “Y” at early to middle layers.
